reference_sql:
SELECT MAX(t.n_orders) AS max_orders
FROM (
  -- one row per registered customer
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
) AS t
alternatives:
WITH customer_orders AS (
  -- one row per registered customer
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT MAX(n_orders) AS max_orders
FROM customer_orders

SELECT MAX(c.n_orders) AS max_orders
FROM (
  -- one row per registered customer
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(order_id) AS n_orders
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
) AS c

other_way.sql:
WITH customer_orders AS (
  -- one row per registered customer
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT MAX(n_orders) AS max_orders
FROM customer_orders
other_way.tradeoff: A WITH step names the per-customer counts before MAX reads them; for one short step the derived table is just as clear.
